rationale: Read the captured design documents for statements that bear on the recorded findings, since requirement anchoring is what separates a defect from a design consequence. Two results: the proposal's statement that a new configuration takes effect as soon as it is appended, together with the at-most-one-uncommitted-configuration rule, closes an earlier suspicion of mine as documented design rather than a defect; and the Voter/Nonvoter definitions independently anchor the requirement behind the non-voter transfer finding. A discrepancy between the proposal and the shipped GetConfiguration documentation is recorded as not-a-defect, because the shipped documentation governs.

investigations.question: Which statements in the captured design documents bear on configuration handling and non-voter participation, and do they contradict a recorded finding or convert one of my earlier suspicions into documented design?
investigations.hypothesis: The membership proposal says a new configuration is in effect as soon as it is appended to the log (not when committed), that at most one configuration may be uncommitted at a time, and that the latest configuration is almost always the one used - which is exactly the commitment behaviour I had considered as a possible progress defect; and it defines Voter versus Nonvoter by participation ('vote is counted in elections and whose match index is used in advancing the commit index' versus 'receives log entries but is not considered for elections or commitment purposes'), which anchors the requirement behind the non-voter transfer finding. One proposal line about GetConfiguration does not match the shipped documentation, but the shipped documentation is the contract.
investigations.discriminator: Refuted as requirement support if the shipped code contradicts those statements without saying so (which would make the document current normative text rather than a proposal), and refuted as a negative if some recorded finding actually depends on a configuration taking effect only at commit; the GetConfiguration point is settled by the shipped doc comment.
limitations: membership.md is a review proposal written before the implementation, not a specification: it even labels its catch-up threshold a placeholder and describes AddVoter as staging-oriented, while the shipped code documents AddVoter as adding a voter and deprecates Staging. It is therefore used only where the shipped code and the API documentation agree with it.
Only the captured documents were read (docs/apply.md, docs/README.md and membership.md); no external specification was consulted, per the run's search restrictions.

knowledge.statement: The captured membership proposal states the intent that governs the behaviour I had flagged as a possible progress defect: a new configuration is in effect as soon as it is appended to the log rather than when it is committed, at most one configuration may be uncommitted at a time, and the latest configuration is almost always the one used (the committed one being needed only when a follower truncates a suffix or when snapshotting). The implementation matches this shape - configuration change requests are gated on the latest configuration being committed, and the commitment configuration is switched when a configuration entry is appended. A consequence of that documented intent is that an uncommitted configuration change can narrow the set whose majority is needed for progress, and the cluster cannot make progress on that change until a majority of the new configuration stores it; that is design behaviour, not a deviation from a stated duty.
knowledge.conditions: Read as the intended design in the captured proposal, corroborated by the shipped gating and commitment behaviour already recorded; the proposal is not itself the shipped contract, so this is intent evidence rather than a normative requirement on the current code.

knowledge.statement: Both captured texts define suffrage by participation: a Voter's vote is counted in elections and its match index is used in advancing the commit index, while a Nonvoter receives log entries but is not considered for elections or commitment purposes. This is independent of the LeadershipTransfer API documentation and states the same expectation that a named non-voting member cannot become leader, which is the requirement the non-voter transfer finding rests on.
knowledge.conditions: The proposal's wording covers the modes it introduced; the shipped code expresses the same distinction through the suffrage field and the election and quorum paths already recorded.

interpretations.rationale: Three outcomes. First, a negative that closes an earlier suspicion of my own: I had considered whether a leader switching its commitment configuration to an uncommitted membership change (so that progress requires a majority of the new configuration, which can be narrower than the still-available majority of the committed one) is a defect. The captured proposal states that a new configuration takes effect as soon as it is appended and that only one configuration may be uncommitted at a time, and that the latest configuration is almost always the one used; the shipped code implements exactly that shape. The behaviour is therefore the documented design of this library, and I record it as a source-explained negative rather than a finding. Second, requirement support for the non-voter transfer finding: the proposal defines a Nonvoter as a member that 'receives log entries but is not considered for elections or commitment purposes', which is the same expectation as the API documentation's graceful-failure promise; the two together make the requirement for that finding doubly anchored in captured material rather than resting on one doc comment. Third, a discrepancy recorded as not-a-defect: the proposal says GetConfiguration waits for the latest configuration to commit and returns the committed one, while the shipped method documents and implements returning the latest configuration, which may be uncommitted. The shipped API documentation is the contract for the shipped code, and the proposal is a historical review document that also differs from the code on other points (it presents AddVoter as staging-oriented and deprecates nothing, whereas the code adds a voter directly and deprecates the staging mode), so this is documentation drift between a proposal and the implementation, not a behavioural defect.
counterevidence: The proposal is not normative for the shipped code; using it as requirement evidence would be wrong wherever the code and the API documentation differ, which is why the GetConfiguration point is excluded.

Its catch-up rule is explicitly labelled a placeholder ('once the staging server has reached 95% of the leader's commit index'), and the shipped code has no such rule, so the document cannot be used to demand behaviour the code does not claim.

The negative about uncommitted configurations does not weaken any recorded finding: the findings that touch membership (the non-voter transfer and the transfer-readiness records) do not depend on a configuration taking effect only at commit.
No execution: this record is about documented intent and its correspondence with already-recorded code behaviour.
limitations: Intent evidence only for the uncommitted-configuration negative; a reviewer who treats membership.md as obsolete would have to re-derive the same conclusion from the code's gating and commitment behaviour, which are recorded separately.
Only the three captured documents were read; nothing outside the snapshot was consulted.
The GetConfiguration drift is noted but not pursued, because no captured statement makes the shipped behaviour a duty violation.
interpretations.report_title: 文档核对：未提交配置“追加即生效”属既定设计；非投票者定义再次锚定转移目标要求
interpretations.report_answer: 本次核对保留的设计文档（仅源码/文档阅读，未执行）。三项结果：其一，把我此前的一个疑点记录为“按设计”的负面结论——membership.md 明确说明新配置在追加到日志时即生效（而非在提交时）、同一时间最多只能有一个未提交配置、且“几乎总是使用 latest 配置”；实现与该形态一致。因此“未提交成员变更会收窄推进所需的多数集合、直到新配置多数落盘前无法推进该变更”属于既定设计，不作为缺陷记录。其二，为“向非投票成员转移领导权”的发现增加了独立的需求锚点：文档把 Nonvoter 定义为“接收日志条目但不参与选举与提交”的成员，与 API 文档“无法晋升时优雅失败”的承诺一致，两条捕获材料共同支持该要求。其三，记录一处文档漂移但不作为缺陷：提案称 GetConfiguration 会等待 latest 提交后返回 committed 配置，而实现与其自身注释返回可能尚未提交的 latest；由于 shipped API 注释才是契约，且该提案在其他方面也与实现不同（如把 AddVoter 描述为 staging 导向），这属于提案与实现之间的文档漂移，而非行为缺陷。限制：membership.md 是历史评审提案而非规范，仅在其与实现/API 文档一致处被采用。
